# Secondary analysis decisions

These are retrospective analyses on public data already studied in the project. We specified the following choices before executing the secondary evaluator. The original G/T release remains frozen.

* OULAD. Train and calibrate on 2013B/J, assigning learners by a deterministic SHA-256 bucket (80/20). Leave out 2014B, whose outcomes need not have matured at 2014J entry. Test on 2014J learners absent from every earlier presentation. In every partition require known registration by day 60 and no withdrawal on or before that day. Use all modules and the released four labels, feature encoding, rolling-sum inputs (days 0 through 60 inclusive), optimizer and default gate. The released active-site feature counts site/day rows, including repeat visits to a site. Fit the vocabulary, scaler and weights on training data only. Estimate both thresholds only on calibration data.
* UCI 697. Use all published labels (Dropout, Enrolled, Graduate), and only admission grade, previous qualification grade, age at enrollment and application order. Use a standardized multinomial logistic classifier, default L2 strength C=1, training-only scaling. Hash the zero-based source row number into 60/20/20 train/calibration/test partitions. Apply the same order-statistic rules, with Dropout as the rerouting target. This tests the decision rule on a different task, with no chronological claim.
* Use the shared logistic classifier's maximum class probability for confidence-only selection at the gate's calibration threshold. Also rank by maximum confidence at 10%, 25%, 50%, 75% and 100% observed capacity, breaking ties by source-file order. Compare rerouted labels to argmax there with the original calibrated rerouting threshold.
* At the gate operating point decompose the gate-minus-unrestricted accuracy difference into the change from labeling the exact accepted cases and the change from selecting them. Separately count differences from the maximum-confidence selector at the gate's capacity. Report coverage, conditional error and the two signed components with paired percentile intervals (2,000 fixed-seed bootstrap resamples of test learners). Hold fits, thresholds and presentations fixed; intervals describe within-cohort sampling only.
